lessons.story:
During review, Lila circles five words: reveal, neutral, revise, excluding, and confirmation. She notices that several recent passages warn readers against giving a word more power than it has. A confirmation number, for example, says a form arrived; it does not announce a prize.

Her first task is to recommend a mystery without revealing its surprise. She describes the writing and leaves the answer to the mystery untouched. For the juice activity, she chooses neutral labels rather than names that suggest one cup should taste better.

Next, she helps a fictional student revise a story. The body contains 182 words, excluding a three-word title. Lila says at least two body words must go to reach a 180-word limit. Deleting only the title would not solve the problem.

She finishes by checking whether the revised entry was actually submitted. A good edit saved on a computer may never reach the judges. Lila's review rule is simple: after understanding a sentence, ask exactly what it establishes and what still requires another action or piece of evidence.
lessons.title: What the Confirmation Cannot Promise
